task: shop for or enroll in a health insurance plan online (healthcare.gov, a state exchange, an employer open-enrollment portal, the Medicare plan finder): enter household and income details where asked, compare plans on premium, deductible, and network, select a plan and proceed toward enrollment; complete when the enrollment confirmation or the plan-selection summary is on screen. Surface pinned: the marketplace or enrollment flow — not insurance-explainer talking heads (that is policyinfo-class content).

tree.label: Get health insurance coverage
tree.note: do 1, with 2 where the venue shows rules and windows - three keepers land straight in the forms and skip 2. then 3, and 4 where drug costs drive the choice (the four Medicare keepers). the middle by regime: 5 on the marketplace routes, 6 on the employer routes, neither on the entitlement route - the benefit is fixed and the work is proving eligibility (iPQr, BEkw). 5 reaches back into 4 and re-reads the list until the configuration settles (fB0o, 5ISG, ma8-). then 7 where an application exists - on the employer routes the elections are the application, so 6 goes straight to 8. then 8, and 9 as far as the venue lets verification run in-session.

children.label: Reach the enrollment system
children.note: 1.1, then whichever entry the venue demands: 1.2 with 1.3 where the portal re-asks inside (mtI4), 1.4 where the login fails or the site allows it (Lwux, all four Medicare keepers), 1.5 on the captcha-only portal, 1.6 when an agent works someone else's case. then 1.7 where enrollment lives behind an event or a banner.

questions.question: Is there a visual countdown timer indicating how much time you have left before the session times out?

questions.check: Does the page ask about current Medicare coverage or drug cost help?

questions.question: Did you need to trigger the informational hover tooltips to read the exact legal definitions for household members or tax dependents?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might answer based on general assumptions without triggering the visual hover state to read the specific legal definition, potentially causing you to misreport your household size.
questions.check: What does the tooltip say counts as a household member or tax dependent?

questions.question: Is your pre-filled personal information accurate and up to date?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to catch and correct outdated personal details like your address or tobacco use status before they are submitted.
questions.check: Do the pre-filled name, birth date and address match what the person gave?
questions.say_example: The form pre-filled your address as <the old one>. You told me <the new one>, so I'm fixing it.

questions.question: What are your gender, full name, and mobile number?
questions.why: The 'Tell us about yourself' section requires this basic personal and contact information to proceed with the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent would not know your exact personal details or which mobile number you prefer to use for the application.
questions.check: Which personal fields does the form ask for?
questions.say_example: I'm filling in your name, gender, and phone number now.

questions.question: What level of medical and prescription drug use should I estimate for the upcoming year?
questions.why: The screen asks you to balance premium costs against out-of-pocket expenses and estimate your expected medical and prescription drug use to filter the available plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might accept the default low-use settings, potentially skewing the plan recommendations away from what would actually be most cost-effective for your specific health needs.
questions.check: What usage levels does the page offer, and what does it apply if left blank?
questions.say_example: The site asks how much care you expect next year, low, medium, or high. It changes the estimates. Skip it and it assumes medium.

questions.question: Do you want to check if your household can save money on coverage costs?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to explicitly choose whether to pursue the cost-savings evaluation path before beginning the application.
questions.check: Does the application offer checking for savings on coverage costs?

questions.question: Is this calculated monthly income right?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to correct the system's zero-dollar estimate and accurately report your unpredictable self-employment income.
questions.check: What monthly income does the page show as calculated?
questions.say_example: The form thinks your monthly income is <$0.00>. Is that right? Your discount rides on this number.

questions.question: Do you have any deductible expenses to report?
questions.why: Claiming deductible expenses like student loan interest or IRA contributions lowers your reported income, which can reduce your monthly premium.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to lower your monthly premium by ensuring all eligible deductions are accurately claimed.
questions.check: Does the page ask about deductible expenses like student loan interest or IRA contributions?
questions.say_example: Do you pay student loan interest, or put money in an IRA? Those lower the income the site counts, and that lowers your bill.

questions.question: Do you have access to health care benefits or an HRA through a job?
questions.why: The application asks about job-based benefits and Health Reimbursement Arrangements to accurately determine your eligibility for financial assistance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent might incorrectly report your access to employer-sponsored coverage, which could result in lost subsidies or future tax penalties.
questions.check: Does the page ask about job-based health benefits or an HRA?
questions.say_example: Does your job offer health coverage or an HRA? The site needs the honest answer to get your discount right.

questions.question: Do I receive financial assistance from programs like Medicaid or Supplemental Security Income?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might not know your current enrollment status in other government assistance programs, potentially leading to inaccurate premium calculations or plan eligibility.
questions.check: Does the page ask about Medicaid, SSI or similar assistance?

questions.question: Does the auto-calculated yearly income match the entered pay rate and frequency?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might blindly input numbers without verifying the visual auto-calculated total, meaning a simple dropdown error (entering annual salary into a monthly field) goes unnoticed and ruins your subsidy eligibility.
questions.check: Does the auto-calculated yearly income match the entered pay rate and frequency?

questions.question: Has the system split your household, directing some members to Medicaid/CHIP and others to the marketplace?
questions.why: Depending on age, income, and state rules, children might be eligible for CHIP while parents get marketplace plans, which drastically changes the enrollment flow and costs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly accept the split without realizing you now have to manage two separate enrollments and provider networks for your family.
questions.check: Does the page route some household members to Medicaid or CHIP and others to marketplace plans?

questions.question: Do you qualify for any financial assistance with your drug costs?

questions.check: Does the page show an Extra Help or assistance status?

questions.question: Did the portal flag a discrepancy between your stated income and IRS records, generating a Data Matching Issue?
questions.why: If your estimated income differs significantly from your last tax return, the exchange requires you to submit recent pay stubs within 90 days or risk losing your financial subsidies.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might ignore the DMI warning, resulting in your premium tax credits being unexpectedly revoked months later.

questions.question: Does the system flag your employer's health plan as 'affordable,' which disqualifies you from subsidies?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might accept the disqualification without giving you the chance to dispute the affordability calculation using the employer coverage tool.
questions.check: Does the page say the employer plan counts as affordable and blocks tax credits?

questions.question: How much of a premium tax credit do you qualify for?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify your exact financial assistance amount and understand how it will offset your monthly premiums.

questions.question: Do you want to continue past the disclaimer to view the results?

questions.check: Does the effective date on the confirmation match the start date expected?
questions.say_example: The confirmation says coverage starts <March 1>, not <February 1>. Enrolling after the 15th pushed it a month. Say the word if that's a problem.

questions.question: Do you want to review your submitted enrollment details and note the deadline for changes?
questions.why: The confirmation page displays your submitted benefit selections and specifies the November 21 deadline for making any further changes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that your final enrollment details are correct and to note the exact deadline for future modifications.
questions.check: What change deadline does the confirmation page state?
questions.say_example: Submitted. You can still change anything until <November 21>. After that it locks for the year.

questions.question: Do you want to print the enrollment summary for your records before navigating away?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Print' button next to the submission confirmation, offering a final chance to save a copy of the completed enrollment details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to keep a printed or saved digital copy of the final enrollment summary for your personal records.
questions.check: Does the page offer printing or saving the confirmation?
questions.say_example: Saved a PDF of the confirmation to your Downloads.

questions.question: Did you note the acknowledgement number for your successful enrollment?
questions.why: The screen displays a success message and a specific acknowledgement number that must be saved to track your application status.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you rely on the agent to securely record and pass on the critical confirmation number needed for your personal records.
questions.check: What acknowledgement number does the success page show?
questions.say_example: Acknowledgement number <XYZ789> saved in the report.

questions.question: What are your next steps after completing the payment?
questions.why: The screen shows a confirmation message with crucial links for downloading your e-Card after 8-10 days and understanding claim procedures.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose immediate awareness of the 8-10 day waiting period and direct access to the links required to download your e-Card.
questions.check: What next steps and timelines does the confirmation give?
questions.say_example: Done. The e-card arrives in <8 to 10 days>, and I saved the claims instructions in the report.

questions.question: Should you check your email inbox to verify the confirmation receipt?
questions.why: The final screen states an email will be sent confirming your elections, but the video ends without verifying it actually arrived.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the definitive proof of enrollment that the confirmation email provides for their personal records.
questions.check: Does the page say a confirmation email will be sent?
questions.say_example: A confirmation email should be coming. I'll check it arrives and that it matches what we chose.

questions.question: How do you verify your application status and retrieve your ID card?
questions.why: The dashboard confirms your enrollment with a 'STATE ACCEPTED' status and provides a sidebar link to download your official ID card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate opportunity to securely download and save a personal copy of your new health insurance ID card.
questions.check: What application status does the dashboard show, and is the ID card available?
questions.say_example: Checked back. The state accepted it, and your ID card is downloaded and in your folder.
